what: The photo is laid down as a black-and-white print (contrast curve .5 mixed into brightness), only a 70px circle around the cursor (14px soft edge) enlarges 1.35× and gets its color back. The loupe follows with a glide at 10 per second and fades out when leaving the panel. On press, a color ripple spreads from that spot to the photo edge in .6s, then returns to black and white.

options.wave: Color ripple duration at the pressed spot (s), default .6
options.follow: Speed at which the magnifier follows the cursor (1/sec), default 10
options.[data-fx-part=img]: Photo — must be the same origin (or CORS-enabled) for WebGL to read it

from.where: strip.js film cell photo face (original loupeR 70 · loupeSoft 14 · loupeMag 1.35 · bwContrast .5 · waveDur .6 · cursorLerp 10 — the original uses the same shader in every cell on a 3D strip)

note: On devices without a hand pointer only the press ripple is applied, without the magnifier. Photos are not hidden — the canvas covers them, so if the script is off the original photo shows.
